mechanism_reasoning: down NANOG is a core pluripotency factor that positively regulates its own promoter — the Nanog locus carries NANOG-binding elements in its upstream enhancer/promoter region, forming a positive autoregulatory loop that sustains high Nanog transcript levels in embryonic stem cells. When NANOG protein is lost or reduced, those activating NANOG–DNA contacts at the Nanog promoter/enhancer are withdrawn, so transcriptional initiation at Nanog drops and, because the loop is self-reinforcing, the reduction is amplified rather than buffered. Order of events: NANOG protein level falls → occupancy of the Nanog regulatory elements decreases → Nanog transcription decreases → Nanog mRNA (and subsequently protein) goes down relative to the matched unperturbed control. Note that the effect is not purely direct: NANOG also activates other pluripotency regulators (OCT4, SOX2) that feed into the same promoter, so part of the drop is indirect through loss of those co-activators.
